## Contaminating $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{j}$ {#sec-sensitivity}

Starting from the fitted sparse precisions (@eq-grn-export), apply the
misspecification factors described in DeCovarT
`vignettes/S5-misspecification.qmd`:

1. Observation noise (Gaussian, $t_\nu$, PLN, contaminated Gaussian)
2. Missing reference component (0%, 2%, 10%)
3. Copula / PLN dependence across genes
4. Spillover between types
5. Outlier genes
6. Wrong covariance reference (perturb or subsample the glasso / PLN fit)

Zero-inflated or hurdle observation models belong **here**, as a
contamination of the sampling layer, not as the default GRN
(@nte-drop-zico).

## `scDesign3` settings for GSE229513 {#sec-sens-scdesign3}

The fitted count simulator of
[S5, simulator](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/S5-misspecification.html#sec-s5-simulator)
draws reference-like cells whose type-level law is known. On
Suppinger it is used to calibrate, not to resample: the cells of one
specimen series are not biological replicates
(@nte-pseudoreplication).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Fit unit | One model per time slot, 48 h, 72 h and 96 h; the two lines pooled at 48 h, cell line not a covariate (@sec-geo-design) |
| Cells and genes | Cells after QC, culture-stress labels removed (@sec-fs-qc); the selected panel, raw UMI counts (@sec-cov-inputs) |
| Margins | Negative binomial, mean and dispersion by cell type, log size factor as mean offset; no zero inflation (@nte-drop-zico) |
| Copula | Gaussian, one per type, correlation of the plug-in $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ of that type and time (@sec-shrinkage); not refitted |
| Composition and depth | Type proportions $C_j/\sum_\ell C_\ell$ of the slot, frozen; each synthetic cell takes the size factor of a real cell of its type |
| Truth for scoring | Count-scale mean and covariance of a large draw (for example $10^{5}$ cells per type), not $\boldsymbol{R}_j$ |
| Checks before use | Normal QQ plots of randomised quantile residuals per gene and type; marginal and copula AIC and BIC against independence and the empirical copula |

: `scDesign3` settings per type and time for GSE229513. {#tbl-sens-scdesign3}

Factors of the list above that the simulator serves:

- **1, observation noise**: negative-binomial cells replace the
  Gaussian law; pseudo-bulks are sums of simulated cells at known
  $\boldsymbol{p}$.
- **2, missing component**: simulate every type and leave one out of
  the signature.
- **3, copula dependence**: swap the plug-in correlation for an
  equicorrelated or a Clayton copula, margins fixed.
- **6, wrong covariance reference**: generate with the
  $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ of one estimator or time, and fit
  DeCovarT with another.

Spillover (4) and outlier genes (5) are added after generation; the
simulator plays no part in them.

```{r}
#| label: sens-scdesign3-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. scDesign3 is not in renv.lock. Function and argument names
# follow the scDesign3 tutorial (modular interface) and must be checked
# against the installed version before use.
# sce: SingleCellExperiment of one time slot, raw UMI counts of the
#   selected panel, culture-stress labels removed; colData holds
#   cell_type and log_s (log size factor).
# sigma_plugin: named list, one G x G plug-in covariance per cell type.
dat <- scDesign3::construct_data(
  sce = sce, assay_use = "counts", celltype = "cell_type",
  pseudotime = NULL, spatial = NULL, other_covariates = "log_s",
  corr_by = "cell_type"
)
marginals <- scDesign3::fit_marginal(
  data = dat, predictor = "gene",
  mu_formula = "cell_type + offset(log_s)",
  sigma_formula = "cell_type",
  family_use = "nb", n_cores = 2, usebam = FALSE
)
para <- scDesign3::extract_para(
  sce = sce, marginal_list = marginals, n_cores = 2,
  family_use = "nb", new_covariate = dat$newCovariate, data = dat$dat
)
# Known dependence: the correlation of each plug-in covariance.
copula_known <- lapply(sigma_plugin, stats::cov2cor)
cells_sim <- scDesign3::simu_new(
  sce = sce, mean_mat = para$mean_mat, sigma_mat = para$sigma_mat,
  zero_mat = para$zero_mat, copula_list = copula_known,
  n_cores = 2, family_use = "nb", input_data = dat$dat,
  new_covariate = dat$newCovariate
)
```

## Signature size and selection threshold {#sec-sens-panel-size}

[S5i, signature size](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/S5-misspecification.html#sec-s5i)
states the hypothesis: accuracy rises with the number of genes, reaches
a plateau, then falls once uninformative genes or genes inconsistent
between bulk and single-cell libraries enter the panel. Every chapter
of this book so far uses one panel, the top `n_genes_global = 500` of
the legacy type-equal `SCTransform` ratio
([legacy type-equal ratio](02-feature-selection.qmd#sec-fs-ms-ratio),
@sec-fs-export). This section
plans the sweep that tests the hypothesis on GSE229513. It has not been
run.

| Factor | Levels |
|---|---|
| Panel size `n_genes_global` | 50; 100; 200; 500; 1000; 2000, the top genes of each rank |
| Rank | legacy type-equal ratio (`ranks_global_equal_type.csv`, column `rank`); omnibus rank, cell-weighted deviance $R^2_D$ (column `deviance_r2`, @sec-fs-omnibus) |
| Omnibus gate | Benjamini–Hochberg level `fdr` of `rank_genes_omnibus()`: 0.001; 0.01; 0.05; 0.2 |
| Bulk consistency filter | off; on (@sec-fs-bulk-consistency) |
| Time slot | 48 h, 72 h, 96 h (@sec-geo-design) |
| Methods | NNLS; DeCovarT, profile Newton (@sec-deconv-models) |

: Factors of the panel-size sweep. The largest panel stays below the size of the allow-list of every slot (@sec-fs-qc). {#tbl-sens-panel-size}

Design choices:

- **Source of genes.** The 500-gene export
  `data/intermediate/equal_type_top500_by_time.rds` cannot supply
  panels larger than 500. The sweep reads the allow-list object
  `data/intermediate/suppinger_sct_allowlist_seurat.rds` and the full
  rank table, then subsets genes per panel size.
- **Truth.** Within each type, cells are split at random into a
  reference half and a pseudo-bulk half. The rank, the mean and the
  covariance use the reference half only; pseudo-bulks are sums of
  cells of the other half at known numbers per type. Bulk and reference
  cells are then disjoint, the condition under which a within-type
  variance can matter
  ([S5, ReDeconv](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/S5-misspecification.html#sec-s5-review-redeconv)).
  Both halves come from one specimen series, so the pseudo-bulks carry
  no platform bias and no between-specimen variation
  (@nte-pseudoreplication).
- **Platform-inconsistent genes.** The pseudo-bulks cannot reveal them.
  The real standard-Wnt bulks of GSE229386 enter through the bulk
  consistency filter: the sweep is repeated on the panels with the
  flagged genes removed, and on the real bulks the change of
  $\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}$ with panel size is reported, since no truth
  exists there.
- **Scale.** Means, covariances and pseudo-bulks use raw UMI counts,
  so a pseudo-bulk is an exact sum of the cell profiles. The
  size-factor scale of @sec-cov-inputs is a second arm.
- **Metrics.** `DeCovarT::compute_benchmark_metrics()` with the true
  cell fractions: total variation and RMSE per bulk
  (`regression$global`), and per-type correlation and error
  (`regression$cell_type`). For the real bulks, the total variation
  between $\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}$ at each size and at 500 genes.

The covariance has $G(G+1)/2$ entries per type. Above the number of
reference cells of a type the sample covariance is singular, and only
the shrinkage estimate of @sec-shrinkage is defined; the closed-form
intensity is used in the sweep rather than cross-validation, to keep the
cost linear in the number of panels.

[TODO: add the level of covariance regularisation as a factor of the
sweep. The shrinkage estimate is dense by construction: it multiplies
every sample correlation by $1 - \lambda$ and sets none to zero, so it
says nothing about isolated groups of genes. At the closed-form
intensity the abundant types are barely shrunk ($\lambda$ of 0.006 to
0.03 on the Welch-gated panels, `output/grn/plugin/plugin_summary.csv`).
Levels to compare: (i) $\lambda$ on a grid, closed form; 0.25; 0.5;
0.75; 1 (diagonal, no gene-gene term); (ii) a sparse arm, the graphical
lasso precision of @eq-grn-export along its penalty path; (iii) raw
counts against size-factor-scaled counts, since a shared cell-size
factor correlates every pair of genes. Report, per type and level, the
share of non-zero off-diagonal partial correlations, the number of
connected components and the condition number, next to the accuracy
metrics and the agreement between the two optimisers. Done so far
(@sec-deconv-96h-diagnosis): level (i) for DeCovarT on the raw
covariance, L-BFGS-B, bulk as is; the RMSE at 96 h on the Welch-gated
panel goes from 0.36 (closed form) to 0.034 ($\lambda=0.5$), with no
gain on the small panels. Levels (ii) and (iii), and a choice of
$\lambda$ that does not use the observed composition, remain.]{.highlight}

```{r}
#| label: sens-panel-size-sweep
#| eval: false
# Not run. Function names and arguments follow R/02_02_stats_cross_cell.R,
# R/03_01_stats_covariance_estimation.R and the DeCovarT reference.
# Culture-stress labels are removed first, as in
# scripts/01_03_export_equal_type_seurat.R.
source("R/02_00_utils.R")
source("R/02_01_stats_quality_control.R")
source("R/02_02_stats_cross_cell.R")
source("R/03_01_stats_covariance_estimation.R")

seu <- readRDS("data/intermediate/suppinger_sct_allowlist_seurat.rds")
ranks <- utils::read.csv(
  "output/naive_marker_selection/tables/ranks_global_equal_type.csv"
)
panel_sizes <- c(50L, 100L, 200L, 500L, 1000L, 2000L)
bh_levels <- c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2)
time_level <- "48h"
n_bulk <- 100L
n_cells_bulk <- 500L

counts <- assay_matrix(seu, "RNA", "counts")
in_slot <- seu$time_point == time_level # & !culture-stress label
x <- as.matrix(counts[, in_slot])
cell_type <- droplevels(factor(seu$celltypeannotation[in_slot]))
lib <- 10^seu$log_umi[in_slot]
types <- levels(cell_type)

# Disjoint halves within each type: 1 = reference, 2 = pseudo-bulk.
half <- withr::with_seed(20261101, {
  stats::ave(
    seq_along(cell_type),
    cell_type,
    FUN = function(i) sample(rep_len(1:2, length(i)))
  )
})
ref <- half == 1L

# Rank A: legacy type-equal ratio of the current panel (computed on all
# cells of the slot; rank B below is the leakage-free one).
rank_a <- ranks[ranks$time_point == time_level & !is.na(ranks$rank), ]
rank_a <- rank_a$gene[order(rank_a$rank)]

# Rank B: omnibus rank on the reference half; fdr = 1 keeps every gene
# so that each BH level is a filter of one fit.
omni <- rank_genes_omnibus(
  x[, ref],
  cell_type[ref],
  size_factors = lib[ref] / stats::median(lib[ref]),
  fdr = 1,
  n_select = max(panel_sizes)
)
omni <- omni[!is.na(omni$rank), ]
rank_b <- lapply(bh_levels, function(level) {
  gated <- omni[omni$adj_pval <= level, ]
  gated$gene[order(gated$rank)]
})
names(rank_b) <- paste0("omnibus_fdr_", bh_levels)

# Pseudo-bulks at known cell numbers, from the pseudo-bulk half.
pseudo <- withr::with_seed(20261102, {
  lapply(seq_len(n_bulk), function(b) {
    w <- stats::rgamma(length(types), shape = 2)
    m <- stats::rmultinom(1L, n_cells_bulk, prob = w / sum(w))[, 1L]
    cells <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(types), function(j) {
      pool <- which(!ref & cell_type == types[j])
      pool[sample.int(length(pool), m[j], replace = TRUE)]
    }))
    list(y = rowSums(x[, cells, drop = FALSE]), p = m / sum(m))
  })
})

fit_panel <- function(genes) {
  mu <- vapply(
    types,
    function(j) rowMeans(x[genes, ref & cell_type == j, drop = FALSE]),
    numeric(length(genes))
  )
  sigma <- vapply(
    types,
    function(j) {
      xj <- t(x[genes, ref & cell_type == j, drop = FALSE])
      fit_cov_shrinkage(xj, lambda = shrinkage_lambda_closed_form(xj))$sigma
    },
    matrix(0, length(genes), length(genes))
  )
  scores <- lapply(pseudo, function(pb) {
    y <- pb$y[genes]
    p_nnls <- DeCovarT::deconvolute_ratios_nnls(y, mu)
    p_dcv <- DeCovarT::deconvolute_single_cell(y, mu, sigma)$p
    rbind(
      cbind(
        method = "nnls",
        DeCovarT::compute_benchmark_metrics(
          y, mu, estimated_p = p_nnls, true_ratios = pb$p
        )$regression$global
      ),
      cbind(
        method = "decovart_newton",
        DeCovarT::compute_benchmark_metrics(
          y, mu, estimated_p = p_dcv, true_ratios = pb$p
        )$regression$global
      )
    )
  })
  do.call(rbind, scores)
}

rank_lists <- c(list(type_equal_ratio = rank_a), rank_b)
sweep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rank_lists), function(r) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(panel_sizes, function(n) {
    genes <- utils::head(rank_lists[[r]], n)
    if (length(genes) < n) {
      return(NULL) # the gate passes fewer genes than requested
    }
    cbind(rank = r, n_genes_global = n, fit_panel(genes))
  }))
}))

# Bulk consistency filter on the real standard-Wnt bulks of the slot
# (bulk: genes x 3 replicates, same identifiers). sd and n_cells come
# from the reference half; flagged genes are removed before the sweep
# is repeated.
# flags <- bulk_consistency_filter(bulk, mu = mu_all, sd = sd_all,
#                                  n_cells = table(cell_type[ref]))
# rank_lists_clean <- lapply(rank_lists, intersect, flags$gene[flags$keep])
```

Three outcomes would bear on the hypothesis. A rise and a plateau in
both methods, with no decline up to 2000 genes, says that the panel of
500 is not too large for the pseudo-bulks. A decline that disappears
after the bulk consistency filter points to platform-inconsistent
genes, which only the real bulks can show. A decline in DeCovarT alone,
present already on pseudo-bulks, points to the covariance estimate
rather than to the genes.
